to.label: Future Arcanum workflow-maintenance agent or owner

subject: Automate Task Session lifecycle hooks after the Body War prototype fast lane
why_now: Manual Invoke Refresh preparation and closeout round trips are making a bounded Work Pack require repeated operator handholding. The Body War prototype needs to finish its remaining validated acceptance work quickly, so lifecycle-bookkeeping automation is deferred to this durable notice rather than treated as a product-development blocker.
key_points: The recorded chain blocked SWU-BWAA-001 when its three live targets changed after baseline capture even though every postimage exactly matched the staged package, the coverage receipt reported 13 flows covering 109 portals, all eight projection tests passed, and scoped diff validation passed.

The failure was lifecycle attribution and synchronization, not a demonstrated product defect: no Task Session terminal receipt existed and the selected inventory no longer bound the observed live preimages.
The current Work Pack records SWU-BWAA-001 and SWU-BWAA-002 as flag-complete, SWU-BWAA-005 and SWU-BWAA-003 as complete, and SWU-BWAA-004 as the sole dependency-ready remaining browser-evidence unit.

The desired operator experience is one Task Session command whose material preparation, exact staged-output reconciliation, and closeout synchronization run as background hooks and join through verifiable receipts without additional user prompts when no substantive conflict exists.
Prototype fast-lane execution may defer lifecycle bookkeeping and later synchronization, but it must retain the declared test, generation, browser, and scoped-diff validation surfaces.

open_calls.question: Which Task Session lifecycle boundaries should launch material preparation and closeout synchronization as automatic background hooks, and what join contract proves each hook finished?

What deterministic rule may reconcile live bytes that exactly equal admitted staged outputs without a user round trip while still preserving writer attribution, inventory binding, and terminal-receipt integrity?

What explicit fast-lane mode can defer non-product lifecycle bookkeeping while remaining fail-closed on validation failures, real byte conflicts, authority expansion, privacy risk, destructive actions, and release or production gates?

boundaries: Do not treat this notice, its locator, or prototype completion as authority, promotion, release, deployment, or production readiness.

Fast-lane execution may defer receipt synchronization, planning-ledger updates, and other lifecycle bookkeeping; it must not skip declared unit or integration tests, generation checks, browser acceptance, scoped diff checks, or defect reporting.

Remain fail-closed for substantive staged-versus-live conflicts, validation failures, destructive actions, privacy or public/private boundary risks, semantic-authority changes, ambiguous successors, and production or release gates.
Keep Body War product implementation separate from the later Arcanum workflow-maintenance change; do not repair generated skill mirrors or canonical public Arcanum sources inside a Body War SWU.
Any automatic hook must emit independently verifiable receipts and surface genuine blockers even if routine synchronization runs silently in the background.

next_actions.action: Design a Task Session prepare hook that creates or refreshes material admission in the background and joins before the first product write.
Design a post-validation closeout hook that synchronizes the Work Pack and continuation cursor without another user invocation.
Specify and test a deterministic exact-staged-output reconciliation path plus a bounded fast-lane policy that preserves all validation and safety ceilings.
After prototype testing, reconcile deferred lifecycle receipts and flag-complete units before any promotion, release, or production claim.
